comparison: Both evaluate claims about additive enhancer combination (C37-C40) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the additive model is favored with exception for Ap1m1. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding, with all reviewers stating the data support near-additive combination. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate claims about near-additive behavior with error model (C41-C44) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative statistical support. Peer reviewers affirm the data support near-additive claims. Strong agreement on this finding.

Both evaluate promoter-dependent supra-additivity (C45-C48) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical correlations and quantitative thresholds. Peer reviewers call this 'interesting and well supported,' identifying it as one of two main findings. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate correlation analyses distinguishing developmental and housekeeping promoters (C55-C58) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes quantitative differences in correlation coefficients. Peer reviewers affirm the finding without critique. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate non-linear promoter scaling (C59-C62) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval identifies this as a key mechanistic finding with quantitative slope analysis. Peer reviewers note alignment with Hong et al. model and accept the negative correlation between scaling steepness and promoter strength. Strong agreement.

Both address single enhancer analysis (C63). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED by Figure 5 supplement 2. Peer reviewer specifically requested this analysis and found adequate data for readers to evaluate the relationship between enhancer boost and promoter strength. Agreement after revision.

Both evaluate power-law interpretation and promoter function (C70-C72). OpenEval finds the inference about exponents <1 reasonably drawn from data. Peer reviewers accept the promoter scaling relationship, with Reviewer 2 finding the equivalence of related figures 'intriguing.' Agreement on interpretation.

Both evaluate promoter selectivity findings (C32-C33) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical confirmation consistent with prior work. Peer reviewers accept this as confirmatory, noting it 'adds another layer' to previous findings. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate replicate reproducibility (C26-C27). OpenEval finds correlation values and interpretation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these quality control metrics as part of 'nice experimental design and great dataset' with no major concerns. Agreement.

Both evaluate single enhancer characterization (C28-C31). OpenEval finds statistical thresholds and analysis SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept technical quality without questioning these methodological details. Agreement on validation findings.

Both evaluate quantitative data on enhancer supra-additivity across promoters (C51-C52) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes specific thresholds and figure references. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings and note revised manuscript 'satisfactorily addresses' related questions. Agreement.

Both evaluate within-locus versus between-locus enhancer comparison (C53-C54) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes no preferential locus-specific synergy. Peer reviewers accept these findings after authors addressed revision requests about supra-additivity patterns. Agreement.

Both evaluate saturation observations (C34-C36, C49-C50). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate qualification. Peer reviewers accept these as nuances within the broader additive model they affirm. Agreement on observations as part of near-additivity finding.

Both evaluate episomal approach methodology (C74-C76, C79). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers acknowledge these methodological features and limitations without challenging validity, noting authors appropriately note limitations. Agreement on methodological validity.

Both address generalizability and potential limitations (C77). OpenEval finds appropriate scientific caution SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note UNCERTAIN regarding which experimental designs preserve non-additivity mechanisms, acknowledging authors 'cannot rule out' certain limitations. Partial agreement with more uncertainty from peer reviewers.

Both evaluate experimental limitations (C80, C82). OpenEval finds acknowledgment SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN about how limitations affect interpretation, noting uncertainty about which mechanisms are preserved. OpenEval more accepting, peer reviewers more cautious.

Both evaluate comparison with prior genomic studies (C83-C87). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats and qualified speculation. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN, explicitly raising discrepancy with Brosh et al. 2023 and noting uncertainty about reconciling findings. Significant disagreement: OpenEval accepts with caveats, peer reviewers uncertain about validity.

Both evaluate two-factor explanation of enhancer-promoter compatibility (C89-C90) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes synthesis of current and prior findings. Peer reviewers accept this interpretation after authors addressed revision requests about reconciling selectivity findings. Agreement after clarification.
